pull_request.head: study/tracker-first-layouts
pull_request.body:
## Executive summary

Retain **cobe** (classical barrel endcap; formerly A) and **pint** (progressive inclined transition; formerly C1) as the only active DES-006 alternatives, following [noemina's expert review](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/13#pullrequestreview-5292271321). B and C2 are withdrawn; their original evidence is preserved. All work remains **DRAFT / isolated PROTOTYPE**, within the retained tracker envelope and `|eta| < 4` study contract.

Read the updated two-page briefs: **[cobe](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/69ea15bd37edb7af44aeb9e9e52688b13c933de9/docs/design/DES-006-reviewed-cobe.pdf)** and **[pint](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/69ea15bd37edb7af44aeb9e9e52688b13c933de9/docs/design/DES-006-reviewed-pint.pdf)**. The [full response matrix](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/69ea15bd37edb7af44aeb9e9e52688b13c933de9/docs/design/DES-006-expert-review.md) addresses all nine expert points and the inline material comments, including unresolved outcomes.

The bounded radial/axial study tests narrower, separated disk bands; first/second pixel radii; outer momentum leverage; barrel/endcap transitions; and eta-spaced/shifted pint rows. At eta=1.1 from the origin, the approximate q/pT uncertainty improves **5.7% / 8.5% for cobe** and **5.9% / 8.7% for pint**, at pT=1 / 100 GeV. The useful mechanism is a longer outer barrel with a nearby first disk, selected jointly with its radius.

**Neither complete iteration is recommended for adoption.** Narrower annuli lose hits: the finer-grid worst q/pT uncertainty ratios to each original option are **1.430 (cobe)** and **1.473 (pint)**. The second-pixel move improves some high-pT IP estimates but worsens central low-pT d0 by about 4%. Eta-spaced pint rows and shifts up to 100 mm were tested; the final gap-constrained choice remains uniform z, so globally constant hit counts remain unresolved. Local gains do not establish overall physics performance.

## What changed

- [Exact current cobe/pint surfaces](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/69ea15bd37edb7af44aeb9e9e52688b13c933de9/docs/design/DES-006-named-layouts.json), drawings and revised two-page briefs; original controls remain unchanged.
- [611 attempted variants and retained profiles](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/06275ecf55e4bb428ffbdb1d5beb72c9a7aca064/docs/validation/DES-006-expert-optimisation.json), with explicit objective, all attempted grid choices, failed pilot disposition and adverse cases.
- Public straight-reference GLS covariance with leading Gaussian thin-scatterer noise, analytic/measurement-only tests and zero/half/nominal/double-material controls. This is not reconstructed resolution or a full material budget.
- [Final cobe IdRes run](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/06275ecf55e4bb428ffbdb1d5beb72c9a7aca064/docs/validation/DES-006-reviewed-A-idres.json): 11 runs and 8,019 finite fit rows. pint is not exported because the adapter does not represent inclined surfaces.
- Precise CMS/ATLAS TDR envelope/beam-pipe comparisons and PDG scattering locators; proposed service-space and pipe-exclusion fixtures are explicitly provisional.
- Expert changes-requested history, current dependencies, curated session record, and repairs to two pre-existing tracking JSON object-boundary errors preserving both tracker and Spack records.

## Validation and limits

Executed 486 search cases per feasible variant, 966 finer covariance profiles per original/iterated option and 21,627 signed finite-field probes per geometry. Geometry probes cover 2/3/4 T, 1/10/100 GeV and vertices −150/0/+150 mm. No sampled grid proves continuous hermeticity. Ideal segment checks find no intersections/host violations; finite modules, support volumes and services are not yet represented.

Passed locally: **29 tracker, 27 dashboard, 32 logging and 5 node-preflight tests; 14 JavaScript assertions**, dashboard validation/build, session validation, retained input/code/source hashes and final whitespace checks. Both PDFs contain two A4 pages; all four pages were visually inspected. The 12 near-zero-material IdRes/control comparisons agree within printed precision, testing the measurement-only limit rather than equality of scattering models. Hosted CI is reported separately on this PR.

## Review priorities and missing inputs

1. Obtain beam-pipe, module/support and service-routing envelopes; 10 mm radial and 30 mm axial reservations are hypotheses, not engineered clearances.
2. Repair narrowed-band transition hit losses before ranking or adopting either complete iteration.
3. Agree physics/beamspot weights and evaluate the inner-two-layer IP tradeoff.
4. Revisit pint row count, row length and module tiling jointly; fixed six-row tests did not settle constant hit counts.
5. Proceed to ACTS navigation/material-aware studies with available field inputs; full simulation follows the later DD4hep/Geant4 integration.

Historical scientific evidence review target: `06275ecf55e4bb428ffbdb1d5beb72c9a7aca064`; a following metadata-only commit records this exact revision. Expert conditions remain open until human confirmation. Final sign-off remains with `asalzburger-review`. Related programme #11; component/field dependencies #7 / #8 / #6. No production integration or human approval is inferred.

## Integration update — 2026-09-25

Rebased onto main `58136c8` and resolved tracking conflicts while preserving main's Spack/publication records and all historical logs. Current named proposal revision: `69ea15bd37edb7af44aeb9e9e52688b13c933de9`. The user requested merge readiness and renamed A → **cobe** (classical barrel endcap), C1 → **pint** (progressive inclined transition). Layer parameters and all historical numerical results are unchanged; the named catalogue carries legacy IDs and its source hash. Two new invariance tests pass; both new briefs contain two A4 pages, all visually checked.

The original PR head remains reachable on [the archive branch](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/tree/archive/pr13-before-rebase-2026-09-25). Existing expert review history and design-signoff boundaries remain intact.

Imported 12 already-curated historical usage turns for all four PR sessions (36,548,583 input / 196,911 output tokens). **The required token-accounting check still fails solely for the current rebase session**, whose completed-turn counters are not available yet. This is not waived by merge readiness or hosted CI; resolve it before merging unless the human explicitly grants an exception.

comments.body:
Very quick feedback on what's there:
- for the measurement count make sure that the long strip modules are double-sided.

Make a more aggressive alternative layout C with inclined modules where it would save material, and compare it to the baseline - charge PhysVal and TrackTec to make a cost-benefit assessment of that.

Hi @noemina - I have added `REVIEW.md` to the main branch with review instructions. Have fun.

Objectives:
- we would like to keep the layout as close as possible to the ODD (to make the shift more smooth for users)
- we want to increase the coverage to |eta| < 4 
- we want to have good hit coverage

Addressed the two technical points in d32da2541415f4730297601e0779594f08f5beaf:

- **Double-sided long strips:** the proposal and executable accounting now distinguish two scalar sensor faces, one paired station and the pair's single material allowance. Both faces enter silicon area. The central example is 10 stations / 12 silicon faces / 20 ideal scalar coordinates; raw IdRes hit counts are labelled separately.
- **Inclined alternative C:** added a [two-page proposal](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/d32da2541415f4730297601e0779594f08f5beaf/docs/design/DES-006-proposal-C.pdf), concrete layer geometry, A/C scans, and independent [TrackTech](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/d32da2541415f4730297601e0779594f08f5beaf/docs/design/inputs/DES-006-inclined-tracktech.md) and [PhysVal](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/d32da2541415f4730297601e0779594f08f5beaf/docs/design/inputs/DES-006-inclined-physval.md) cost–benefit assessments. C lowers ideal strixel area by 9.13% and double-sided long-strip area by 1.96%, with no parent-station loss in the declared scan. Local material varies from −22.1% to +23.7% relative to A, so overlap penalties are retained in the recommendation.

The recommendation is to pursue tiled inclined-strixel studies first while retaining A as control; the smaller long-strip benefit needs an engineering justification. C's forward pixels are unchanged, and no C IdRes resolution is claimed. Eighteen prototype tests pass; the proposal, evidence and executive summary are updated for your review.

The inclined Long strips look a bit complicated for the actual gain. I wonder if it is worth it to introduce such a level of complexity for the outermost 2 barrel layer, where the incident angle is not very dramatic.

Plesae split C into C1 (only short strip inclined) and C2 (both inclined) - this should give us enouth to chose from.

Another question:
- how much optimisation did you put into the actual radial postions and z-positions of the layers already ?

Split C as requested in 8b7604ea27075038baa18050ba5ab1d6ab48e622:

- **[C1](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/8b7604ea27075038baa18050ba5ab1d6ab48e622/docs/design/DES-006-proposal-C1.pdf):** only short-strip barrel ends inclined; both long-strip barrels remain cylindrical as in A.
- **[C2](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/8b7604ea27075038baa18050ba5ab1d6ab48e622/docs/design/DES-006-proposal-C2.pdf):** short and long strips inclined, identical to the original C geometry.

Both retain the 9.13% ideal strixel-area saving. C2 adds 24 inclined long-strip row envelopes for just 1.96% less ideal long-strip silicon area (2.196 m², including both faces). The sampled local-material range relative to A is 0.779–1.117 for C1 versus 0.779–1.237 for C2. Neither loses parent stations in the declared scans. This supports investigating the simpler C1 first while keeping C2 available for the engineering/physics decision.

On radial and z-position optimisation: **no systematic optimisation has been done yet**. Barrel radii were retained from ODD. Barrel lengths, disk positions and annuli were hand-chosen starting hypotheses to extend coverage and test transitions; A/B compare two fixed forward-pixel hypotheses. C used a geometric pointing prescription and a small 0/5/10 mm overlap study. Field/material/vertex sweeps are sensitivity checks, not position searches, and C1/C2 do not retune positions. There is no objective-function search or claim of optimal placement.

The [detailed response](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/8b7604ea27075038baa18050ba5ab1d6ab48e622/docs/design/DES-006-C1-C2-review.md) records what was varied, what remains unoptimised, and the constraints needed for a useful next scan. Drawings, separate two-page briefs, A/C1/C2 evidence and the PR executive summary are updated. All 61 local tests pass; no layout is selected.
drop this option. The large radial overlap between the disks looks too complicated to handle, also for the services routing and detector/volume separations. DES-006-A is better in this regards.
This would also results into more material in some specific eta regions (e.g. between eta=2 and eta=3)
The slightly worse pT resolution for pT=1GeV in  2.5<|eta|<3.5 could be explained by the increase in amount of material indeed, as mentioned in the comment above.

I have a few comments to consider for an additional step in the review process:
- Only keep option A and option C1. 
- Considering the information on the subsystem envelopes from the technical design reports, optimise the spacing between the volumes.
- Evaluate the impact on the number of hits for the innermost disks. Having these disks going to larger R, slightly overlapping with the middle disks is engineering more complicated, and would add complications in the routing of the services from the barrel as well. 
- For both option iteratively improve the radial spacing between the different layers considering the impact on the physics performance, mainly resolutions on the track parameters. 
- The position of the innermost hit (and next to innermost hit) strongly impacts the IP resolution. Consider the beampipe limits (also compare with the technical design reports) to come up with sensible and realistic numbers. The position of the innermost hit is crucial when moving also in the forward region where we move from cylinders to disks.
- The position of the outermost hit has effect on the momentum resolution, so try to improve on the coverage of the last hit position as well.
- Optimise the distance between the barrel layers and the endcap disks: the longer is the distance between these regions, the more is complicated to reconstruct the track. Also this is a critical region since in general this is also where service are routed from the barrel to the outermost part of the endcap. Less extrapolation region is therefore preferable.
- For the inclined region in C, optimise the placement of the inclined layers in z to maintain a constant number of hits as a function of eta (more far apart when moving towards higher eta values). The position in R of the full row of inclined modules can also be slightly (max ~10cm) shifted wrt the flat region if required to fill holes in the coverage. Though it is important the different objects do not clash.
- Propose a solution to recover momentum resolution at eta~1.1

Addressed the expert review in `06275ecf55e4bb428ffbdb1d5beb72c9a7aca064`. Only **A and C1** remain active; the PR summary and their two-page briefs now reflect that scope.

The [point-by-point response and results](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/06275ecf55e4bb428ffbdb1d5beb72c9a7aca064/docs/design/DES-006-expert-review.md) cover TDR envelope comparisons, reduced overlap, first/second and last hits, radial/axial optimisation, service transitions, inclined-row spacing/shifts and eta=1.1 recovery. All attempted bounded scans and original controls are retained.

The outer-transition change improves the origin eta=1.1 q/pT uncertainty by roughly 6–9% in the stated Gaussian model. However, narrower bands lose hits elsewhere and the worst local q/pT regressions remain 43% / 47% for A / C1. Therefore neither complete iteration is proposed for adoption. C1 eta-spaced rows were tested, but the guarded choice remains uniform z: constant hit counts and real module/service clearances remain open.

B's forward material concern is documented conditionally; separating disk-count and annulus-width effects is still needed for unique attribution. Beam-pipe/support/service profiles and agreed physics weights remain missing inputs, not inferred engineering facts.

Local tests/builds pass, including 27 tracker tests and the IdRes measurement-only cross-check. Please re-review the response and priority order, particularly transition repair and C1 tiling. I have retained the changes-requested decision and have not marked human conditions resolved or recorded sign-off.
Decision: we move forward with A and C1 as alternatives. This PR can be merged (after conflict resolving), refinement will be done once module decisions and local support is better defined.
Ok, fine-tuning will then be done once module and local support is established.
After discussing with @noemina we move to the next stage, keeping A and C1.

## Executive summary

Retain **cobe** (classical barrel endcap; formerly A) and **pint** (progressive inclined transition; formerly C1) as the only active DES-006 alternatives, following [noemina's expert review](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/13#pullrequestreview-5292271321). B and C2 are withdrawn; their original evidence is preserved. All work remains **DRAFT / isolated PROTOTYPE**, within the retained tracker envelope and `|eta| < 4` study contract.

Read the updated two-page briefs: **[cobe](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/69ea15bd37edb7af44aeb9e9e52688b13c933de9/docs/design/DES-006-reviewed-cobe.pdf)** and **[pint](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/69ea15bd37edb7af44aeb9e9e52688b13c933de9/docs/design/DES-006-reviewed-pint.pdf)**. The [full response matrix](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/69ea15bd37edb7af44aeb9e9e52688b13c933de9/docs/design/DES-006-expert-review.md) addresses all nine expert points and the inline material comments, including unresolved outcomes.

The bounded radial/axial study tests narrower, separated disk bands; first/second pixel radii; outer momentum leverage; barrel/endcap transitions; and eta-spaced/shifted pint rows. At eta=1.1 from the origin, the approximate q/pT uncertainty improves **5.7% / 8.5% for cobe** and **5.9% / 8.7% for pint**, at pT=1 / 100 GeV. The useful mechanism is a longer outer barrel with a nearby first disk, selected jointly with its radius.

**Neither complete iteration is recommended for adoption.** Narrower annuli lose hits: the finer-grid worst q/pT uncertainty ratios to each original option are **1.430 (cobe)** and **1.473 (pint)**. The second-pixel move improves some high-pT IP estimates but worsens central low-pT d0 by about 4%. Eta-spaced pint rows and shifts up to 100 mm were tested; the final gap-constrained choice remains uniform z, so globally constant hit counts remain unresolved. Local gains do not establish overall physics performance.

## What changed

- [Exact current cobe/pint surfaces](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/69ea15bd37edb7af44aeb9e9e52688b13c933de9/docs/design/DES-006-named-layouts.json), drawings and revised two-page briefs; original controls remain unchanged.
- [611 attempted variants and retained profiles](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/06275ecf55e4bb428ffbdb1d5beb72c9a7aca064/docs/validation/DES-006-expert-optimisation.json), with explicit objective, all attempted grid choices, failed pilot disposition and adverse cases.
- Public straight-reference GLS covariance with leading Gaussian thin-scatterer noise, analytic/measurement-only tests and zero/half/nominal/double-material controls. This is not reconstructed resolution or a full material budget.
- [Final cobe IdRes run](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/06275ecf55e4bb428ffbdb1d5beb72c9a7aca064/docs/validation/DES-006-reviewed-A-idres.json): 11 runs and 8,019 finite fit rows. pint is not exported because the adapter does not represent inclined surfaces.
- Precise CMS/ATLAS TDR envelope/beam-pipe comparisons and PDG scattering locators; proposed service-space and pipe-exclusion fixtures are explicitly provisional.
- Expert changes-requested history, current dependencies, curated session record, and repairs to two pre-existing tracking JSON object-boundary errors preserving both tracker and Spack records.

## Validation and limits

Executed 486 search cases per feasible variant, 966 finer covariance profiles per original/iterated option and 21,627 signed finite-field probes per geometry. Geometry probes cover 2/3/4 T, 1/10/100 GeV and vertices −150/0/+150 mm. No sampled grid proves continuous hermeticity. Ideal segment checks find no intersections/host violations; finite modules, support volumes and services are not yet represented.

Passed locally: **29 tracker, 27 dashboard, 32 logging and 5 node-preflight tests; 14 JavaScript assertions**, dashboard validation/build, session validation, retained input/code/source hashes and final whitespace checks. Both PDFs contain two A4 pages; all four pages were visually inspected. The 12 near-zero-material IdRes/control comparisons agree within printed precision, testing the measurement-only limit rather than equality of scattering models. Hosted CI is reported separately on this PR.

## Review priorities and missing inputs

1. Obtain beam-pipe, module/support and service-routing envelopes; 10 mm radial and 30 mm axial reservations are hypotheses, not engineered clearances.
2. Repair narrowed-band transition hit losses before ranking or adopting either complete iteration.
3. Agree physics/beamspot weights and evaluate the inner-two-layer IP tradeoff.
4. Revisit pint row count, row length and module tiling jointly; fixed six-row tests did not settle constant hit counts.
5. Proceed to ACTS navigation/material-aware studies with available field inputs; full simulation follows the later DD4hep/Geant4 integration.

Historical scientific evidence review target: `06275ecf55e4bb428ffbdb1d5beb72c9a7aca064`; a following metadata-only commit records this exact revision. Expert conditions remain open until human confirmation. Final sign-off remains with `asalzburger-review`. Related programme #11; component/field dependencies #7 / #8 / #6. No production integration or human approval is inferred.

## Integration update — 2026-09-25

Rebased onto main `58136c8` and resolved tracking conflicts while preserving main's Spack/publication records and all historical logs. Current named proposal revision: `69ea15bd37edb7af44aeb9e9e52688b13c933de9`. The user requested merge readiness and renamed A → **cobe** (classical barrel endcap), C1 → **pint** (progressive inclined transition). Layer parameters and all historical numerical results are unchanged; the named catalogue carries legacy IDs and its source hash. Two new invariance tests pass; both new briefs contain two A4 pages, all visually checked.

The original PR head remains reachable on [the archive branch](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/tree/archive/pr13-before-rebase-2026-09-25). Existing expert review history and design-signoff boundaries remain intact.

Imported 12 already-curated historical usage turns for all four PR sessions (36,548,583 input / 196,911 output tokens). **The required token-accounting check still fails solely for the current rebase session**, whose completed-turn counters are not available yet. This is not waived by merge readiness or hosted CI; resolve it before merging unless the human explicitly grants an exception.

Very quick feedback on what's there:
- for the measurement count make sure that the long strip modules are double-sided.

Make a more aggressive alternative layout C with inclined modules where it would save material, and compare it to the baseline - charge PhysVal and TrackTec to make a cost-benefit assessment of that.

Hi @noemina - I have added `REVIEW.md` to the main branch with review instructions. Have fun.

Objectives:
- we would like to keep the layout as close as possible to the ODD (to make the shift more smooth for users)
- we want to increase the coverage to |eta| < 4 
- we want to have good hit coverage

Addressed the two technical points in d32da2541415f4730297601e0779594f08f5beaf:

- **Double-sided long strips:** the proposal and executable accounting now distinguish two scalar sensor faces, one paired station and the pair's single material allowance. Both faces enter silicon area. The central example is 10 stations / 12 silicon faces / 20 ideal scalar coordinates; raw IdRes hit counts are labelled separately.
- **Inclined alternative C:** added a [two-page proposal](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/d32da2541415f4730297601e0779594f08f5beaf/docs/design/DES-006-proposal-C.pdf), concrete layer geometry, A/C scans, and independent [TrackTech](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/d32da2541415f4730297601e0779594f08f5beaf/docs/design/inputs/DES-006-inclined-tracktech.md) and [PhysVal](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/d32da2541415f4730297601e0779594f08f5beaf/docs/design/inputs/DES-006-inclined-physval.md) cost–benefit assessments. C lowers ideal strixel area by 9.13% and double-sided long-strip area by 1.96%, with no parent-station loss in the declared scan. Local material varies from −22.1% to +23.7% relative to A, so overlap penalties are retained in the recommendation.

The recommendation is to pursue tiled inclined-strixel studies first while retaining A as control; the smaller long-strip benefit needs an engineering justification. C's forward pixels are unchanged, and no C IdRes resolution is claimed. Eighteen prototype tests pass; the proposal, evidence and executive summary are updated for your review.

The inclined Long strips look a bit complicated for the actual gain. I wonder if it is worth it to introduce such a level of complexity for the outermost 2 barrel layer, where the incident angle is not very dramatic.

Plesae split C into C1 (only short strip inclined) and C2 (both inclined) - this should give us enouth to chose from.

Another question:
- how much optimisation did you put into the actual radial postions and z-positions of the layers already ?

Split C as requested in 8b7604ea27075038baa18050ba5ab1d6ab48e622:

- **[C1](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/8b7604ea27075038baa18050ba5ab1d6ab48e622/docs/design/DES-006-proposal-C1.pdf):** only short-strip barrel ends inclined; both long-strip barrels remain cylindrical as in A.
- **[C2](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/8b7604ea27075038baa18050ba5ab1d6ab48e622/docs/design/DES-006-proposal-C2.pdf):** short and long strips inclined, identical to the original C geometry.

Both retain the 9.13% ideal strixel-area saving. C2 adds 24 inclined long-strip row envelopes for just 1.96% less ideal long-strip silicon area (2.196 m², including both faces). The sampled local-material range relative to A is 0.779–1.117 for C1 versus 0.779–1.237 for C2. Neither loses parent stations in the declared scans. This supports investigating the simpler C1 first while keeping C2 available for the engineering/physics decision.

On radial and z-position optimisation: **no systematic optimisation has been done yet**. Barrel radii were retained from ODD. Barrel lengths, disk positions and annuli were hand-chosen starting hypotheses to extend coverage and test transitions; A/B compare two fixed forward-pixel hypotheses. C used a geometric pointing prescription and a small 0/5/10 mm overlap study. Field/material/vertex sweeps are sensitivity checks, not position searches, and C1/C2 do not retune positions. There is no objective-function search or claim of optimal placement.
